- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if recent history shows volatility.
- Model often overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment, producing exaggerated overshoots in 30-day forecasts; cap or dampen forecasts after 3–5 consecutive high sentiment days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model tends to underperform; adjust downward bias by 10–20% in early horizon (1–7 days) if sentiment is flat.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates after sharp spikes, then underestimates in follow-up; apply smoothing or decay factor to forecasts after 3+ consecutive high values.
- For long horizon (15–30 days), model often fails to capture sentiment-driven mean reversion; reduce forecast by 15–30% if sentiment turns negative or neutral after a spike.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.00 or negative), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% in 1–3 day horizon to compensate for sentiment lag.
